thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Continuous-batching service experiencing a perf cliff under high concurrency. KV cache growth and queueing spike detected. metric: cb_tail_latency_99 = 3.1s (+x10), queue_length ~ 2400, cpu@workers ~ 92%. Auto-mitigation not triggered.

alex: Ack. I'm on it — pinging sanjay and mira. What changed recently?

sanjay: I saw a config rollback PR earlier that removed jitter and bumped microbatch size for throughput tests (PR #4523). Could be related.

mira: Confirming: yesterday we merged a change to continuous-batching default microbatch_tokens=256 -> 512, and jitter_pct reduced from 0.2 -> 0.0 to get deterministic p99 for internal tests.

alex: That matches. High concurrency + larger microbatches = queue lockups and KV cache blowup due to long-lived KV shards. Initial triage: 1) throttle ingress 2) hotfix batching config back to safe values 3) restart workers gracefully to trim KV cache.

leah: Agreed. Customer impact: error_rate for /v1/generate-highcon current = 11.8% (was 0.2%). Three enterprise customers reported timeouts. Notified CSE.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: inc-20260317-1763401234 severity=P1 tags: continuous-batching, kv-cache, customer-impact

alex: Quick plan: apply hotfix config -> set microbatch_tokens=128, jitter_pct=0.18, max_batch_delay_ms=10, max_concurrency=600 for the autoscaler cap. Then rolling restart of worker pools with graceful drain.

ryan: I can push the hotfix. Will route through /internal/config API. Command I will run:

```
# patch batching config for service continuous-batching
curl -X PATCH https://internal-config.redwood/api/v1/services/continuous-batching -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"batching": {"microbatch_tokens": 128, "jitter_pct": 0.18, "max_batch_delay_ms": 10}}'
```

alex: Before you push, capture current metrics and create a quick canary on 10% of workers. We want to avoid full rollback that could spike latency elsewhere.

ryan: Got it. Applying to canary set now (canary label=hotfix-cb-176340).

sanjay: Note: KV cache eviction policy has a bug where LRU pointers aren't updated when microbatch durations exceed 1s. That makes cache retention pathological under bigger microbatches. We should avoid bigger microbatches until fix.

mira: I'm taking over primary oncall at 03:15 UTC. If mitigation needs follow-up, escalate to storage team.

alex: Update: canary hotfix applied. Observing queue_length drop on canary from 800 -> 120, cb_tail_latency_99 from 2.6s -> 0.45s. Putting hotfix into rollout for 50% now.

leah: Customer ops note: opened support tickets for the three affected customers and sent an interim status message: "We’re mitigating a performance degradation impacting high-concurrency workloads; reduced impact expected within 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:

ryan: Rolling to 50% done. Will continue to 100% if metrics stay stable for 5 mins.

alex: While rolling, I'm going to throttle a small percentage of new high-concurrency requests at the edge to buy time: set rate_limit override for tier-highcon to 60% of normal.

ops-bot: RATE LIMIT UPDATE: applied rate_limit override to tier-highcon = 60% by alex

sanjay: I pushed a minimal code fix branch to address LRU pointer update. Will prep a patch for next deploy but hotfix config is the right immediate action.

mira: Monitoring logs for KV OOMs and eviction counts. If eviction count doesn't increase within 2 mins, we should force a graceful restart for old workers.

alex: 10 minute check: overall error_rate down to 1.9%, cb_tail_latency_99 = 0.6s cluster-wide, queue_length avg = 180. Looks good. Recommend full rollout to 100% and schedule postmortem.

ryan: Hotfix rolled to 100%. Performing worker restart wave to flush stale KV shards (rolling, 10 pods at a time):
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batching -n inference --selector=worker-pool=cb --grace-period=60
```

leah: Confirmed customer-facing messages updated. CS is asking for ETA on full recovery and root cause.

alex: ETA: recovery stabilizing now; we'll run 15m observation window. Root cause preliminary: config change that removed jitter + increased microbatch size exposed a latent bug in KV eviction logic leading to cache blowups under high concurrency. Severity P1 -> downgrade to P2 after stable 15m.

mira: Taking the handoff. I'll own the postmortem, assign to sanjay (root cause), ryan (deployment changes), and infra (LRU eviction tests). Adding follow-ups: add canary gating for batching config changes, add synthetic high-concurrency workload to CI, fix LRU pointer bug, add autoscaler backpressure when queue_length > threshold.

alex: Thanks. Final note: retention of this thread for postmortem. Nice quick work everyone. :clap:

ryan: Leaving a short command history for audit:
```
PATCH /internal-config/services/continuous-batching {microbatch_tokens:128,jitter_pct:0.18,max_batch_delay_ms:10}
kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batching (rolling 10 pods)
applied rate limit override tier-highcon=60%
```

mira: Marking incident inc-20260317-1763401234 as mitigated pending 15m stable window.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: inc-20260317-1763401234 status=mitigated monitored_until=1763404355

alex: (adding one more) we'll run a follow-up runbook update to include microbatch safe thresholds and an automated trigger to reduce microbatch size when queue_length spikes.

leah: Thanks all. Handoff complete.
